_note: GX-00 D3D8 device/resource method census (roadmap parity-evidence §9 GX-00). The v3 capture proxy (tools/trace_studio_v3/proxy/) wraps IDirect3D8 + IDirect3DDevice8; each vtable slot is either INTERCEPTED (a hand-written my_<Iface>_<Name> that records the call into the container) or a generated PASS-THROUGH forwarder (fwd_<Iface>_<Name>, proxy_generated.h). This file is the R3 CENSUS: every method's capture_class, so a render-affecting method that is silently forwarded (uncaptured) cannot hide — the truthful-evidence prerequisite for a sound `pixels`/`render_program` pillar (a replay is only complete if every render-affecting call the game makes was recorded). Consumed by tools/parity/d3d_census.py; the drift guard tools/test_d3d_census.py asserts proxy_generated.h's actual recorded/forwarded split matches this census (a method flipping recorded<->forwarded, or added/removed by a d3d8.h/gen_forwarders change, fails the test). This is the STATIC census (which methods CAN affect pixels); the DYNAMIC census (which are actually CALLED in a capture — 0 observed => safe, >0 => must record-or-fail) is the GX-00 follow-up that needs a proxy call-counter + a drive. Classification policy (GX-01) is FAIL-CLOSED: a forwarded method that CAN alter future pixels/resources/device state is `render_affecting_unsupported` (a capture-completeness RISK), never `forwarded_irrelevant`, unless proven visually inert.

capture_classes.recorded: a my_ interceptor records the call's render effect into the container (draws, fixed-function state setters, Clear/Present, SetRenderTarget/CopyRects, CreateTexture, CreateDevice params). The replay reproduces it.
capture_classes.wrapper_lifetime: a my_ interceptor for COM plumbing only (QueryInterface/AddRef/Release) — needed to keep the wrapper identity, no render effect, nothing to replay.
capture_classes.query_only: a forwarded READ (Get*/Check*/Test*/Validate*/GetInfo) — returns info, changes no device state, cannot affect future pixels. Safe to forward.
capture_classes.forwarded_irrelevant: a forwarded call proven visually inert (pure memory/handle management — ResourceManagerDiscardBytes, a Delete* that frees a handle, RegisterSoftwareDevice). Safe to forward.
capture_classes.render_affecting_unsupported: a forwarded call that CAN alter future pixels / resources / device state but is NOT recorded — a capture-completeness RISK. If the game calls one, the replay may diverge silently. GX-01 must make these record-or-FAIL; GX-02 implements the ones actually observed. Fail-closed default for anything render-affecting.

risk_subgroups._note: the render_affecting_unsupported set of IDirect3DDevice8, grouped for the GX-01/GX-02 record-or-fail order (roadmap high-risk seed list). Recettear is a 2007 DX8 fixed-function game so most are likely NEVER called — the DYNAMIC census confirms which; until then they are STATIC risks a call would silently drop.

leads.shader_binding_asymmetry: SetVertexShader is RECORDED but SetPixelShader is FORWARDED (uncaptured) — an asymmetry. In D3D8 fixed-function these 'shader' handles are the FVF/programmable toggle; if the game ever binds a pixel shader the replay would miss it while catching the vertex-shader change. Verify via the dynamic census whether SetPixelShader is ever called (likely not in this title, but the asymmetry is a real capture-completeness gap).
